🔮 About

Emoji Games is a corner of The White Witch™ (@TheWhiteWitchTM). Old terminal games, redrawn with emoji, played in the page you already have open.

Politics broke me, so I started porting old games. Then I got bored of those too and decided the emojis needed their own corner. This is that corner.

The rules

No accounts.
No “please create an account to play a 50-year-old idea with pictures.”
No quiet sponsors.
Argue with the code, not the caption.

The games run in your browser. Nothing on this site asks who you are.

How to play

Open a game. The picture is the emoji engine. Return leaves the title. R starts that game again and skips the title.

Pong is the left paddle. W and S, or the arrows. First to 5.

Snake turns with the arrows or WASD. One hundred points clears the board. A crash ends it.

Adventureland, Pirate Adventure, and Galaxy Hunt want words. Type a command and press Return. HELP prints what that game understands. RESTART begins again. From the last screen, R does it without the title.

Rogue and Hack are dungeons. You move a step at a time. In Rogue, Q drinks a potion. In Hack, P drinks one, and the Amulet of Yendor is on the sixth floor.

Trump Super Intelligence is a conversation, not a match. There is no title card and no game over. Type a line and press Return. The face changes with the mood.

The Oregon Trail opens on a title. Return goes to the menu. R from that title, or from a finished trail, starts the next party without showing the title again. On the road, Return stops the wagon. Hunt and the Columbia raft use the arrows.

Witch I is a computer. Boot fills the screen, and she stays there until Escape ends the session. The prompt is SPEAK. A line number stores a line. RUN starts the program. SHELF opens the box, and the arrows take a program down. LIST shows the lines. PEEK and POKE make her complain. Ctrl-C stops one that will not stop. Basic I is the same glass, and the prompt is READY. Boot works the same way.

What shipped

12 October 2026. Pong and Snake. Two games you can explain in a sentence, which made them the right place to start. Notes.

13 October. Galaxy Hunt, Adventureland, and Pirate Adventure. A starship, then two treasure hunts that want you to type. Notes.

14 October. Rogue and Hack. Same family. Rogue is a single room and an amulet on the sixth floor. Hack is rooms, corridors, and a bestiary that gets meaner as you go down. Notes.

15 October. Quiet.

16 October. Trump Super Intelligence. Not a port. You type, it answers, the picture of the face swaps. Notes. The Oregon Trail. A wagon, five names, and the road to the Willamette. Notes. Witch I. A 40-column machine that speaks WASIC. Notes.

17 October. Basic I. The same glass as Witch I, and the prompt is READY. Notes.

Witch I, the add-on. She did not ship twice. The shelf points, Enter takes a program down, LIST shows the lines, she draws herself when she wakes, and EXORCISE drives BASIC out of a listing. Notes.

The same day, the other games moved onto the emoji engine. A title waits for Return. Win or death waits for R, and that R skips the title. Galaxy Hunt, The Oregon Trail, and Hack lead the menu and the catalog. Trump Super Intelligence stays a conversation. Notes.

18 October. The desk. Play or Boot, a manual beside it, the banner under the buttons, and the words under the banner. Notes.

The catalog is how you browse. The release notes are the log.
